adds.title: Transgender prisoners challenge prison authorities (GroundUp)
adds.summary: GroundUp news feature (6 Aug 2025, Elna Schutz) documenting where transgender prisoners are held in South Africa: Jade September, a transgender woman, was imprisoned in the male section of Pollsmoor and won her 2019 Equality Court case against the Minister of Correctional Services, which ruled that not allowing her to express her gender identity was unfair discrimination. Reports that the resulting Department of Correctional Services standard operating procedure (SOP) for LGBT+ prisoners requires a safety-risk assessment within the first six hours of admission and stipulates that transgender men and transgender women are to be detained or transported only with other transgender men or transgender women respectively, alongside respectful-search and communication rules. Also notes Lawyers for Human Rights representation of 'NM', a transgender woman serving a long-term sentence at Johannesburg Correctional Centre, in litigation against DCS over gender-affirming healthcare, and rights organisations' concern about implementation of the SOP.

adds.title: Nthabiseng Mokoena v Head of Johannesburg Correctional Centre - Lawyers for Human Rights
adds.summary: Lawyers for Human Rights case page (14 Nov 2025): the South African High Court, sitting as an Equality Court, ruled in favour of transgender inmate Nthabiseng Mokoena against the Department of Correctional Services (DCS), finding unfair discrimination and harassment because DCS refused to allow her to express her gender identity (feminizing attire, she/her pronouns) and failed to provide appropriate accommodation. The court held that the constitutional right to adequate medical treatment includes gender-affirming hormonal therapy at State expense, rejected DCS's contrary argument, and ordered DCS to immediately implement accommodations, enforce its own SOPs relating to transgender inmates, and provide the prescribed medical care. Subject-verified: documents that trans inmates are accommodated inside the standard national corrections system (here Johannesburg Correctional Centre) and that placement/accommodation obligations rest on DCS SOPs enforced through litigation.

adds.title: Media Statement: National Preventive Mechanism welcomes the High Court ruling affirming the rights of transgender persons in correctional facilities (SAHRC)
adds.summary: South African Human Rights Commission, acting as the National Preventive Mechanism under OPCAT (designated 4 Dec 2024), media statement (14 Nov 2025) welcoming the Gauteng Division of the High Court, Johannesburg, judgment (delivered 10 Nov 2025) in Nthabiseng Beverly Mokoena v Head of Johannesburg Correctional Centre and Others (Case No. 2024/070075). Describes Mokoena, assigned male at birth and identifying as female from early childhood, being restricted from wearing feminine clothing and makeup and misgendered while in a correctional facility. Subject-verified: an official state human-rights body confirming that transgender persons are held in the ordinary correctional system and that the 2025 ruling affirms their rights in correctional facilities, including accommodation.

records.note: South Africa has no gender-identity-based statutory placement regime for transgender prisoners; placement runs through the national Department of Correctional Services under birth-sex segregated facilities plus a court-ordered SOP. The SOP (born of Jade September's 2019 Equality Court win, when she was held in the male section of Pollsmoor) requires a safety-risk assessment within the first six hours of admission and, as of the August 2025 GroundUp report, provides that transgender men and transgender women be detained or transported only with other transgender men or transgender women respectively. The November 2025 High Court judgment in Nthabiseng Mokoena v Head of Johannesburg Correctional Centre (welcome statement by the SAHRC National Preventive Mechanism) found DCS's failure to provide appropriate accommodation discriminatory and ordered DCS to enforce its own transgender-inmate SOPs and provide gender-affirming care. No KwaZulu-Natal-specific custody rule, trans unit, or litigation was located within budget; provincial placement follows this national policy. This record's prior data lacked prison-housing content; the gap is here filled with subject-verified sources.

records.note: Prison-housing for transgender people in South Africa is set by the national Department of Correctional Services, not by province: standard birth-sex segregated facilities under a court-ordered SOP requiring a safety-risk assessment within the first six hours of admission and (per the August 2025 GroundUp report) detention/transport of transgender men and women only with other transgender people of the same gender identity. The November 2025 High Court judgment in Nthabiseng Mokoena v Head of Johannesburg Correctional Centre (welcomed by the SAHRC National Preventive Mechanism) found failure to provide appropriate accommodation for a transgender inmate to be unfair discrimination and ordered DCS to implement its own transgender-inmate SOPs and provide gender-affirming care. No Northern Cape-specific custody rule, trans unit, case, or ruling was located within budget; placement of trans prisoners in the province follows this national policy, and the record's prior prison-housing data gap is here filled with subject-verified sources.
